items.headline: Three dead after supply boat sinks off Pasir Panjang Terminal in collision
items.summary: Three crew members aged 38 to 53 were found dead after a supply boat collided with a landing craft and sank off Pasir Panjang Terminal at about 9.30am on June 12; MPA said search-and-rescue and diving operations continued for anyone still missing.

items.headline: Heavy downpours end Singapore's warm spell, bringing 2026's coolest day
items.summary: Heavy rain on June 12 brought Singapore its coolest day of 2026 so far, ending a prolonged warm, dry stretch as the inter-monsoon period gave way to wetter weather.

items.headline: PM Wong to deliver National Day Rally on Aug 23
items.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong will deliver his 2026 National Day Rally address on Aug 23, the annual keynote that sets out the government's major policy directions for the year ahead.

items.headline: India marks one year since the Air India AI-171 crash that killed 260
items.summary: Families gathered at the Ahmedabad crash site on June 12 to mark a year since Air India flight AI-171, a London-bound Boeing 787, crashed seconds after take-off and killed 260 people, including 19 on the ground, with only one survivor; the final report remains pending.

items.headline: IMD issues red alert for Delhi as storms and heavy rain sweep 15 states
items.summary: The IMD put Delhi under a red alert on June 12 for thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds, and issued rain and storm warnings across about 15 states including Uttar Pradesh and Bihar; Kerala's Ernakulam and Idukki districts were under an orange alert for very heavy rain.

items.headline: FSSAI issues notices to Nestle, KFC and Flipkart over hygiene complaints
items.summary: India's food regulator FSSAI issued notices to Nestle India, KFC India and Flipkart on June 12 after social-media complaints alleging infestation in a Maggi pack, insects in a Flipkart Minutes order and unhygienic conditions at a KFC outlet in Andhra Pradesh; Nestle rejected the Maggi allegation.

items.headline: Indian shares slip and rupee weakens as Middle East tensions and outflows weigh
items.summary: Indian equities eased on June 12, with the Sensex slipping toward 73,800 amid elevated crude prices and persistent foreign-investor selling; the rupee stayed under pressure near 95.5 per US dollar, with year-to-date foreign outflows at a record near US$30 billion.

items.headline: Update: Pakistan says final text of US-Iran deal reached as Trump eyes weekend signing
items.summary: Pakistan's prime minister said mediators had reached a final, agreed-upon text to end the US-Iran war on June 12, and Iran's FM Araghchi said a deal had never been closer; Trump said it could be signed in Europe over the weekend with VP JD Vance attending, though Iran's supreme leader had yet to sign off and Israel said it was not a party.

items.headline: China arrests US scholar Min Zin on suspicion of espionage
items.summary: China's foreign ministry confirmed on June 12 that it had placed Min Zin, a US citizen who heads the Myanmar-focused Institute for Strategy and Policy, under criminal detention on suspicion of espionage; he was detained on arrival at Kunming airport on June 3.

items.headline: Canada earn first World Cup point in 1-1 draw with Bosnia as USA open at home
items.summary: Co-hosts Canada earned their first-ever World Cup point on June 12, with substitute Cyle Larin equalising in the 78th minute for a 1-1 draw against Bosnia and Herzegovina after Sasa Lukic had scored; the United States began their home tournament against Paraguay later the same day.

items.headline: Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM blockade pushes Mali's junta into deepening crisis
items.summary: A months-long fuel blockade by the al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM has squeezed Mali's capital Bamako, with residents queuing for scarce fuel and electricity reportedly cut to about six hours a day, piling pressure on General Assimi Goita's junta and prompting foreign governments to urge citizens to leave.

items.headline: OpenAI acquires cloud startup Ona to power long-running Codex agents
items.summary: OpenAI said on June 11 it would acquire Ona, the German cloud startup formerly known as Gitpod, to let its Codex coding agent run longer, persistent tasks in secure sandboxes; terms were undisclosed and OpenAI said more than 5 million people use Codex weekly.

items.headline: Jeff Bezos's Prometheus raises $12 billion at a $41 billion valuation
items.summary: Prometheus, the physical-AI startup co-founded by Jeff Bezos and Vik Bajaj, said on June 11 it had raised $12 billion at a $41 billion valuation from backers including Bezos, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and BlackRock, to build an 'artificial general engineer' for designing and manufacturing physical systems.

items.headline: Datadog veterans launch AI coding startup Niteshift with $7 million seed
items.summary: Niteshift, founded by former Datadog engineers, launched on June 10 with a $7 million seed round led by Greylock's Jerry Chen and angels including Reid Hoffman and Datadog CEO Olivier Pomel, pitching an AI coding agent built as a bet against single-provider lock-in.

items.headline: Jedify raises $24 million to give AI agents business context
items.summary: Enterprise startup Jedify raised $24 million in a Series A led by Norwest on June 10 to help companies feed AI agents structured context about their operations, part of a wave of funding aimed at making autonomous agents production-ready.

items.headline: Update: SpaceX soars 19% in record stock-market debut
items.summary: SpaceX shares jumped about 19% to close at $160.95 in their June 12 Nasdaq debut under the ticker SPCX, after the company priced the largest IPO in history at $135 a share to raise roughly $75 billion and value the rocket maker near $1.8 trillion; the stock touched $176 intraday.

items.headline: Update: Wall Street rises a second day on US-Iran peace hopes
items.summary: US stocks extended gains on June 12 as investors bet on a US-Iran deal and cheered SpaceX's debut: the S&P 500 rose 0.5% to 7,431.46, the Dow added 353.51 points (0.7%) to 51,202.26 and the Nasdaq gained 0.31% to 25,888.84, leaving the indexes higher for the week.

items.headline: US Justice Department clears Paramount's $110 billion Warner Bros takeover
items.summary: The US Justice Department's antitrust division has cleared Paramount Skydance's roughly $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery without conditions, Politico reported on June 12; California and other states are preparing a lawsuit that could still challenge the deal.

items.headline: Update: Oil extends slide toward $85 as US-Iran deal nears Hormuz reopening
items.summary: Crude prices fell about 2% on June 12, sliding toward the mid-$80s, as hopes that a US-Iran agreement would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift sanctions unwound more of the war-risk premium that had driven oil higher this month.

items.headline: Boulter stuns top seed Rybakina to reach Queen's semi-finals
items.summary: British wildcard Katie Boulter beat world No. 2 and top seed Elena Rybakina 7-5, 2-6, 7-5 at Queen's on June 12 for the biggest win of her career, reaching the semi-finals where she will face Donna Vekic.

items.headline: Teenager Jovic beats Anisimova for first top-five win at Queen's
items.summary: Iva Jovic, 18, beat Wimbledon finalist and second seed Amanda Anisimova 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 at Queen's on June 12 for her first top-five win, reaching the semi-finals of the grass-court WTA 500 event.

items.headline: Vekic downs Pliskova to complete Queen's semi-final lineup
items.summary: Donna Vekic beat former world No. 1 Karolina Pliskova 6-4, 4-6, 6-3 at Queen's on June 12 to reach the semi-finals, setting up a last-four meeting with home favourite Katie Boulter.

items.headline: India begin first-ever ODI series against Afghanistan in Dharamsala
items.summary: India open a three-match ODI series against Afghanistan in Dharamsala on June 13, their first bilateral ODI series against the side, with Shubman Gill leading a new-look attack missing Virat Kohli, Hardik Pandya, Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj.

fun_fact.headline: Honey never spoils
fun_fact.body: Honey is one of the only foods that essentially never spoils; pots of honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs over 3,000 years old were still edible. Its longevity comes from very low moisture, natural acidity, and bee-added enzymes that produce hydrogen peroxide, leaving no environment for microbes to survive.

puzzle.title: The Mislabeled Boxes
puzzle.body: Three boxes contain only apples, only oranges, and a mix of both. Each is labelled Apples, Oranges, or Apples & Oranges, but every label is wrong. Drawing one fruit from one box without looking, what is the fewest draws needed to label all three correctly, and how?
puzzle.approach: Every label is guaranteed wrong; start with the box whose wrong label is most informative.
puzzle.answer: One draw, from the box labelled Apples & Oranges. Since that label is wrong, the box is pure; the fruit you draw names it, and the remaining two boxes are forced by elimination because their labels are also wrong.
